title: Mouse Without Borders Portable 1.0.1-rc.12
summary: Acknowledge drag/drop startup, retry connection timeouts correctly, and show overall transfer size, speed and ETA.
changes: Start new drag/drop transfers over the acknowledged transfer connection; missing or expired selections return an error instead of silently disappearing.
Treat the private 10-second connection timeout as an I/O interruption eligible for the existing bounded retries. Preserve explicit user cancellation.
Show total bytes, combined active copy speed and estimated remaining time in folder groups and the overall list. Suppress misleading ETA when work is paused, cancelled or needs attention.
Record preparation stages and retry reasons in the bounded Mini Log. Preserve the RC11 settings layout.
testing: Update BOTH PCs to RC12. Drag the same multi-file selection several times into disposable destinations; confirm both transfer windows appear and every file arrives.
Copy a folder with many small files and a few large files. Check folder and overall size/speed/ETA, and confirm the completed file count and contents.
Cancel while Preparing, then start another transfer. Confirm the cancelled selection does not start later.
Temporarily disconnect during a disposable transfer; reconnect and check retries or an explicit error/paused state. Confirm Retry resumes and existing files are preserved.
Recheck pause/resume, duplicate filenames, mouse/keyboard sharing, clipboard, lock/unlock and sleep/wake. Capture both Mini Logs if any file needs attention.
known_limitations: This is a candidate fix. Automated checks do not confirm the intermittent real-PC startup problem is resolved.
RC12 requires the other PC to advertise acknowledged startup for new incoming drags; update both PCs. Existing protocol-2 file jobs retain their format.
ETA estimates copying at current speed and does not predict verification time. Short files may finish before a speed estimate settles.
Four outgoing transfers remain the limit. Full-speed Wi-Fi transfers can still cause mouse lag.
